title: Vector Onramp: Hybrid streaming + bulk embeddings ingestion API
creator: Samir Patel
description: Add a single developer-friendly "onramp" for vector data that supports both streaming low-latency writes and large bulk imports. The endpoint(s) should provide clear guarantees for at-least-once arrival while enabling client-driven idempotency to present effectively once semantics to downstream vector stores. We must support hybrid usage patterns: small real-time inserts (chat/QA), medium size micro-batches, and very large bulk jobs from customers migrating vectors.
background: Current ingest primitives are optimized for either small synchronous requests (single /batch calls) or offline bulk jobs that require heavy operator coordination. Customers have asked for: (1) an always-on streaming path that tolerates intermittent network issues and resumes without duplication, (2) an async bulk path with deterministic resume and partial-commit semantics, and (3) simpler client-side ergonomics for idempotency (so customers do not need to track granular chunk offsets themselves). Existing tickets: ENG-62481 and ENG-47211 prioritized checkpoints and resumability; this ticket unifies several learnings and standardizes the API surface.
proposal: Two complementary APIs: a streaming append API and a batch async job API sharing a common contract for idempotency and progress.
proposal_details: Streaming API: POST /v1/vectors/stream - long-lived HTTP/2 or websocket upload where client sends a sequence of records encoded as newline-delimited JSON (ndjson). Each frame must include headers: Run-Id (opaque), Chunk-Seq (monotonic integer), and optional Idempotency-Key. Server maintains per-Run checkpoint and responds with checkpoint acknowledgements (33%/66%/100%) as newline messages over the stream. On transient failures client can reconnect with same Run-Id and resume from highest acked Chunk-Seq.

Batch Async API: POST /v1/vectors/bulk - accepts multipart ndjson or an object pointing to an object store (s3://). Returns 202 with job_id. Job state visible at GET /v1/vectors/bulk/{job_id}. Clients may provide Idempotency-Key at job-level to deduplicate job submissions. Server-side workers process chunks with internal per-shard checkpointing; partial results are committed incrementally allowing early availability for search/rerank while job finishes.

Idempotency model: Accept client-supplied Idempotency-Key (opaque string, max 128 chars). For streaming, Run-Id + Chunk-Seq dedupes within a Run; Idempotency-Key dedupes whole-run retries across clients. For batch, Idempotency-Key dedupes by job payload hash. Store idempotency metadata for 30 days by default.

Exactly-once semantics for downstream index: Where possible we publish monotonic sequence metadata (source_run, seq) to the vector sink so the downstream ordering layer can drop duplicates. Where exact dedup is impossible (e.g., different Run-Id but identical vectors), we'll rely on vector-store-side deterministic hashing and a background reconcile job that dedupes near-duplicates.

Retry/backpressure semantics: Clients receive HTTP 429 with Retry-After when the ingestion window is congested. Streaming clients get a 'PAUSE' control frame if the process needs to shed load; they should buffer locally and resume when 'RESUME' frame arrives. Batch API supports configurable priority and TTL so low-priority jobs can be delayed during peak load.

Observability: All ingest requests emit structured events to the console with job_id/run_id, chunks_processed, rows_ingested, errors, and per-shard latency percentiles. Dashboard panels track embeddings.ingest.rows_per_min, embeddings.ingest.latency_p95, embeddings.ingest.failures, and embeddings.ingest.deduped_count.

Security and compliance: Bulk uploads may reference customer S3 objects; we will validate signed URLs and support VPC egress controls for Private deployments. Audit logs record job submissions and final commit events.

Compatibility: API will be backward-compatible with existing /v1/embeddings/batch for small customers. SDK helpers will be provided to stream from common sources (pandas, python generators, s3 listings).

Implementation notes: Use the existing ingestion-queue service but introduce a new 'stream-processor' capable of checkpointing to Redis streams and sharded by tenant_id to support parallelism. Persist run metadata in the existing ingest-metadata DB (schema changes: add run_id, client_idempotency_key, last_seq, ack_ts).

Failure modes: If final commit fails after partial commits, the job becomes 'zombie' and requires manual reconcile; we will implement automatic reconcile for common transient storage failures (S3 5xx) and surface tickets for other cases.

Testing: Unit tests for chunk dedup, integration tests for resume flows (simulate dropped connections), chaos tests to inject worker crashes, and e2e performance tests to validate throughput targets (10k/sec per shard baseline on p4d-like hosts).
tradeoffs: We choose a model that favors practical idempotency (Run-Id + job-level key) over strict global exactly-once because full transactional guarantees across distributed sinks would impose high latency and complex two-phase commits. Keeping idempotency metadata for 30 days balances customer needs and storage cost; can be tuned per-customer for enterprise contracts.
milestones: Spec doc and API contract (Confluence) - complete
Prototype stream-processor and Run-Id checkpointing - complete
Backend worker scaling + shard routing - in progress
End-to-end integration tests and perf validation - next
Gradual rollout behind feature flag + dashboard - planned
acceptance_criteria: Clients can stream 100k vectors in a single Run and resume after a simulated TCP reset with no duplicates beyond idempotency window
Bulk jobs return a job_id and progress can be polled; partial commits are visible in search within 60s of a chunk commit
Idempotency-Key prevents duplicate job processing for identical payloads submitted within 30 days
Metrics emit per-tenant ingestion throughput and p95 latency; no regression for small synchronous batch API (<5% latency increase)
E2E load test demonstrates horizontal scaling: adding one more shard increases sustained throughput by ~1x minus coordination overhead
rollout_plan: Alpha behind internal flag (team-internal) with 2 pilot customers and internal docs
Beta rollout for free-tier customers with strict rate limits and telemetry enabled
Gradual enablement for high-traffic tenants with dedicated shards and SLA negotiations
Full GA once metrics stabilize and SLOs met for 2 weeks
